title: Christmas cake with a fruit-and-nut top
subtitle: A rich dark fruit cake finished with whole nuts and glacé cherries, no marzipan
excerpt: This version of Christmas cake skips the traditional marzipan and royal icing in favour of whole almonds, Brazil nuts, walnuts, and glacé cherries arranged across the top before baking. The nuts toast as the cake bakes and the cherries sink slightly into the surface. It is less formal than an iced cake and slices cleanly from the tin.
sourceNotes: Fruit-and-nut-topped fruit cakes appear in British baking tradition from at least the late Victorian period. Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136, documents rich fruit cakes of this type. The decorative nut-and-cherry top is a well-established alternative to the marzipan-and-icing finish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Wrap tightly in two layers of cling film and freeze for up to 6 months. Defrost overnight at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The cake improves with age. Bake up to 8 weeks ahead and feed with brandy every week.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional oven; fan 130°C, low and slow prevents the outside from overcooking before the centre is set

glossaryTerms.definition: Adding a small amount of brandy, whisky, or other spirit to a baked fruit cake by pricking the surface and drizzling the spirit over it. Feeding adds flavour and moisture and preserves the cake for weeks.

content.text: A Christmas cake with a fruit-and-nut top is the traditional alternative to the iced version. Whole almonds, Brazil nuts, walnuts, and glacé cherries are pressed into the surface before baking. The nuts toast and the cherries caramelise slightly. The result is beautiful and requires no icing skills.

attrs.prepNote: halved; plus 50 g whole cherries for the top

content.text: Combine the sultanas, raisins, currants, halved glacé cherries, and mixed peel in a bowl. Pour over the brandy, stir, cover, and leave overnight. The fruit plumps and absorbs the spirit. If you do not have time, simmer the fruit and brandy in a saucepan over low heat for 5 minutes and leave to cool.

Double-line a 23 cm round tin with baking paper on the base and sides, coming 5 cm above the rim. Tie a double layer of brown paper around the outside of the tin to protect the sides during the long bake.

Beat the butter and sugar until pale and slightly fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well between additions. Fold in the flour, spices, and ground almonds. Add the treacle, then fold in the soaked fruit and any liquid in the bowl. Spoon into the prepared tin and level. Arrange the whole nuts and whole glacé cherries across the surface, pressing them in lightly.

Bake at 150°C (conventional) for 3 hours 30 minutes to 4 hours. At 3 hours, check with a skewer through the centre, it should come out clean. The top should be deep brown. If the top is colouring too fast before the centre is set, cover loosely with foil.
When the cake is completely cold, prick the base all over with a skewer and drizzle 2 tablespoons of brandy over it. Wrap tightly in baking paper, then in foil.
